Underwater lighting preparation may include forming shells, wet-niche and dry-niche fixtures, conduits extending from forming shells, junction boxes, deck boxes, grounding and bonding connections, and requirements for equipment installed in wet locations. Candidates should review the relationship among the forming shell, raceway, junction box, fixture, and bonding conductor. The SP-SP scope permits certain installation activities involving forming shells and conduits but does not authorize all electrical connections associated with the lighting system. The examination may also include questions involving spas, hot tubs, fountains, and similar installations when the relevant NEC provisions are related to swimming pool bonding concepts. Candidates should know when general pool rules apply and when a separate section governs a particular installation. Business and law preparation may include contractor licensing, application requirements, listed qualified individual responsibilities, license use, contracts, estimating, project scheduling, financial controls, insurance, safety programs, recordkeeping, permits, inspections, and prohibited conduct. Open Book Test The North Carolina Special Restricted Swimming Pool Bonding Contractor examination is an open-book test. The 2020 National Electrical Code is the only reference from this package allowed in the examination room for the SP-SP classification. The Electrical Contractors Licensing Law, Board rules, and NASCLA business reference are included for closed-book preparation. Candidates should study these materials before test day because licensing and business questions must be answered without consulting them during the examination. The NEC may be brought in a softbound, spiral-bound, or hardbound format. Loose-leaf references and incomplete copies are not allowed. The reference may be highlighted, underlined, and annotated before the examination. Notes written in pencil must be highlighted. Notes written in pen do not need to be highlighted. Candidates may not write in the reference during the examination session. Permanent tabs may be used when they comply with current testing requirements. Temporary tabs, removable notes, divider tabs, loose sheets, attached papers, and unauthorized inserts are not permitted. Open-book testing still requires strong reference-navigation skills, especially because the SP-SP examination allows only one hour. Candidates should know how to move quickly to the NEC article covering swimming pools, fountains, and similar installations. Practice should include using the NEC index, table of contents, definitions, article structure, tables, exceptions, and cross-references. Candidates should learn where to locate equipotential bonding requirements, underwater lighting provisions, junction-box rules, grounding provisions, and installation requirements for conductive parts near pools. A question involving the minimum size of a swimming pool bonding conductor may require a specific bonding provision. A question involving underwater lighting may require several related sections addressing forming shells, raceways, junction boxes, fixtures, grounding, and bonding. Candidates should read complete sections rather than relying on a single sentence. Nearby exceptions, installation conditions, material requirements, or location restrictions may affect the correct answer. Timed practice is particularly important for this examination. A useful method is to identify the subject, locate the applicable NEC section, confirm the complete requirement, and answer without spending unnecessary time searching unrelated articles. Licensing Steps Confirm the SP-SP classification. Review the restricted scope and determine whether it matches the swimming pool bonding work the applicant intends to perform. Document qualifying experience. Collect records showing the required primary, secondary, or other recognized electrical and swimming pool experience. Confirm the swimming pool business relationship. The applicant must be primarily engaged in or regularly employed by a lawful swimming pool business in North Carolina and prepared to serve as its listed qualified individual. Complete the examination application. Submit the required personal, employment, experience, and business information to the North Carolina State Board of Examiners of Electrical Contractors. Provide character statements. Include written statements from the required individuals attesting to the applicant’s good character. Submit experience verification. Provide records and statements documenting qualifying electrical or swimming pool field experience. Submit the examination fee. Include the applicable payment with the completed application. Receive Board approval. The Board reviews the application and determines whether the applicant meets the examination requirements. Receive examination authorization. Approved candidates receive a Notice of Approval and PSI eligibility information. Schedule the examination. Register with PSI and choose a testing appointment within the authorized period. Prepare the 2020 NEC. Confirm that the reference complies with current rules involving binding, highlighting, notes, and permanent tabs. Complete the examination. Bring the required identification and approved NEC reference to the testing center. Complete the licensing process. After passing, satisfy the remaining Board requirements for the individual or business entity seeking the SP-SP license. Maintain the license. Follow current renewal, continuing education, listed qualified individual, supervision, and compliance requirements. State Requirements The North Carolina State Board of Examiners of Electrical Contractors regulates the SP-SP examination and license. The Board establishes applicant qualifications, reviews experience, authorizes examinations, issues licenses, and enforces the Electrical Contractors Licensing Law and related rules. An applicant for the Special Restricted Swimming Pool classification must document at least 3,000 hours of qualifying experience. At least 2,000 hours must be primary experience. The remaining hours may consist of primary experience, secondary experience, or a combination of both. Applicants may receive credit for qualifying experience gained in the swimming pool field when that work falls within categories recognized by the Board. The experience must be documented according to the examination application requirements. The applicant must also verify that the applicant is primarily engaged in or regularly employed by a lawful swimming pool business in North Carolina and will serve as the listed qualified individual for that business. The SP-SP license authorizes swimming pool bonding work only as an incident to the license holder’s business of installing, maintaining, or repairing swimming pools. The authorized scope includes bonding required metal parts on or near a swimming pool installation. These parts include metal components of the pool structure, reinforcing metal in the pool shell, coping stones and deck components, forming shells, metal fittings within or attached to the pool structure, metal conduit, metal piping, and fixed metal parts. The scope also includes installation of a common bonding grid that interconnects the required conductive parts. An SP-SP license holder may install forming shells for lighting fixtures and underwater audio equipment. The license also permits installation of conduits extending from lighting-fixture and audio-equipment forming shells to deck boxes or junction boxes, including installation of those boxes. The license holder may install lighting fixtures and audio equipment in their forming shells and extend the appropriate leads to the deck or junction boxes so circuit conductors can be connected by others. The scope also includes installation of a bonding conductor from its connection point at the common bonding grid to a readily accessible point at the circulating pump location. The SP-SP license does not authorize general electrical contracting. It does not permit the license holder to perform electrical work outside the specific swimming pool bonding and related activities established by the Board’s rules. Special restricted classifications are not subject to the project-value limits that apply to regular Limited and Intermediate electrical contractor licenses. The absence of a project-value limit does not expand the type of work authorized under the SP-SP classification. Listed qualified individuals in the SP-SP classification must complete the applicable continuing education required for license renewal. License holders must also comply with requirements involving supervision, business operation, advertising, renewal, and changes in business or employment status. Passing the examination does not independently authorize contracting. The proper license must be issued and active before the individual or business performs or offers to perform work requiring the SP-SP classification. It is not allowed in the examination room. NASCLA Contractors’ Guide to Business, Law, and Project Management: North Carolina Electrical EditionThis closed-book study reference supports preparation involving business organization, contracts, estimating, financial management, project administration, employment practices, safety, insurance, recordkeeping, and risk management. It is not allowed in the examination room. Exam Room Approved Books National Electrical Code, NEC, 2020This is the only reference from the package allowed in the examination room for the North Carolina Special Restricted Swimming Pool Bonding Contractor examination. Test Information and Study Materials Build a study plan around equipotential bonding, conductive pool shells, reinforcing metal, perimeter surfaces, metal fittings, ladders, handrails, fixed metal parts, underwater lighting, forming shells, conduits, junction boxes, licensing law, Board rules, and contractor business practices. Use the 2020 NEC to review the required bonding components, conductor sizes, connection methods, corrosion resistance, continuity, accessibility, and installation requirements around pools and similar locations. Practice identifying the difference between parts that must be bonded and equipment that must be grounded. These concepts are related but serve different purposes and are governed by different Code provisions. Review underwater lighting requirements as a complete system. Study forming shells, raceways, deck boxes, junction boxes, fixture leads, bonding, grounding, and separation from other wiring. Use timed reference-navigation exercises because the examination allows only one hour. Read the question, identify the bonding or pool-equipment subject, locate the applicable section, and verify the complete requirement before answering. Study the licensing law and Board rules separately because they are not available during the examination. Focus on applicant qualifications, the SP-SP scope, listed qualified individual responsibilities, license use, renewal, continuing education, and prohibited conduct. Review the NASCLA business reference for contracts, estimates, scheduling, financial controls, employment responsibilities, insurance, safety administration, project documentation, and risk management. How 1 Exam Prep Helps You Reach Your Goal 1 Exam Prep helps North Carolina Special Restricted Swimming Pool Bonding Contractor candidates organize technical, licensing, and business references into a practical preparation structure. Trade-focused review connects National Electrical Code requirements with swimming pool bonding work, including equipotential bonding grids, reinforcing metal, conductive shells, metal fittings, perimeter surfaces, forming shells, junction boxes, and bonding conductors. Practice-oriented preparation helps candidates identify the subject of a question, locate the applicable NEC section, review the governing requirement, and apply the information efficiently. Reference-navigation practice builds familiarity with the 2020 NEC index, definitions, articles, tables, exceptions, and cross-references. These skills are especially valuable during the one-hour open-book examination. Closed-book study guidance helps candidates review the Electrical Contractors Licensing Law, Board rules, restricted SP-SP scope, experience requirements, and business-management subjects that cannot be referenced during the test. Confidence-building study structure helps candidates divide the examination into manageable technical, regulatory, and business sections while maintaining consistent preparation. No book package can guarantee examination passage or license issuance. Results depend on the candidate’s experience, qualifications, preparation, familiarity with the NEC, understanding of swimming pool bonding systems, and performance during the examination. Frequently Asked Questions What books are included in this package? The package includes the 2020 National Electrical Code, Electrical Contractors Licensing Law, the Board’s electrical contracting rules, and the NASCLA Contractors’ Guide to Business, Law, and Project Management: North Carolina Electrical Edition. Is the SP-SP examination open book? Yes. The examination is open book, but only the approved 2020 National Electrical Code may be used in the examination room. Are the licensing law, Board rules, and NASCLA book allowed in the examination room? No. Those references are included for closed-book study and are not allowed in the testing room. How many questions are on the examination? The North Carolina Special Restricted Swimming Pool Bonding Contractor examination contains 25 multiple-choice questions. How much time is allowed? Candidates have a maximum of one hour to complete the examination. How much experience is required? Applicants must document at least 3,000 hours of qualifying experience, including at least 2,000 hours of primary experience. What work does the SP-SP license authorize? Can the license holder install underwater lighting forming shells? Yes. The authorized scope includes installation of forming shells for lighting fixtures and underwater audio equipment. Can the license holder connect branch-circuit conductors? Is there a project-value limit? No. Special restricted classifications are not subject to the project-value limits that apply to regular Limited and Intermediate licenses, but all work must remain within the SP-SP scope. Does passing the examination automatically issue the license? No. Passing satisfies the examination requirement, but the applicant must complete the Board’s licensing process before performing work under the SP-SP classification.

description: North Carolina Unlimited Electrical Contractor Exam Book Package Prepare for the North Carolina Unlimited Electrical Contractor examination with a comprehensive book package covering commercial, industrial, institutional, residential, and large-scale electrical installations. The North Carolina Unlimited electrical contractor classification is the state’s broadest regular electrical contracting license. It allows a properly licensed contractor to engage in electrical contracting projects regardless of project value, provided the work is performed under an active license and complies with applicable electrical codes, permitting requirements, inspection rules, and professional obligations. This package includes the 2020 National Electrical Code and NFPA 72, National Fire Alarm and Signaling Code, 2019 Edition. These technical references support preparation for questions involving electrical installations, power distribution, fire alarm systems, signaling circuits, motors, generators, transformers, grounding, bonding, conductor sizing, raceways, equipment protection, emergency systems, and system calculations. These closed-book references address North Carolina licensing requirements, qualified-individual responsibilities, license classifications, prohibited practices, contracts, estimating, financial management, project scheduling, employment practices, insurance, safety, recordkeeping, and contractor business administration. Unlimited electrical work may involve complex projects with multiple distribution systems, large services, panelboards, switchboards, transformers, motor loads, emergency systems, fire alarm systems, special occupancies, hazardous locations, lighting systems, and extensive plans and specifications. Successful preparation requires more than memorizing isolated Code rules. Candidates should understand how multiple NEC articles work together and how to apply those requirements to realistic project conditions. The North Carolina Unlimited Electrical Contractor examination is open book for the approved technical references. Candidates may use the 2020 NEC and NFPA 72, 2019 Edition, during the examination. The licensing law, Board rules, and NASCLA business reference are included for closed-book preparation and cannot be consulted during the test. This book package provides the technical, legal, and business references needed to build a structured preparation plan for the North Carolina Unlimited Electrical Contractor examination. It is designed for experienced electrical professionals preparing to demonstrate advanced technical knowledge, supervisory ability, code-navigation skills, and an understanding of electrical contracting responsibilities. Exam Details The North Carolina Unlimited Electrical Contractor examination contains 100 multiple-choice questions. Candidates have a maximum of six hours to complete the examination, and a minimum score of 70 percent is required to pass. The examination is administered through PSI after the North Carolina State Board of Examiners of Electrical Contractors approves the applicant. The exam may involve the National Electrical Code, NFPA 72, electrical plans, specifications, calculations, permits, inspections, licensing law, Board rules, estimating, and business practices. Service and feeder preparation may include load calculations, service conductor sizing, service equipment, disconnecting means, grounding electrode conductors, grounded conductors, parallel conductors, transformer secondaries, feeder demand factors, voltage drop, and protection of conductors and equipment. Branch-circuit preparation should include conductor ampacity, continuous loads, receptacle and lighting loads, appliance circuits, multiwire branch circuits, overcurrent protection, conductor identification, voltage limitations, and requirements for specific occupancies or equipment. Motor questions may involve full-load current, branch-circuit conductor sizing, feeder sizing, overload protection, short-circuit and ground-fault protection, controllers, disconnecting means, duty ratings, multimotor installations, and the correct use of NEC motor tables. Transformer preparation may include primary and secondary conductor sizing, overcurrent protection, grounding and bonding, separately derived systems, transformer vaults, ventilation, clearances, installations in buildings, and secondary-system calculations. Grounding and bonding questions may involve grounding electrode systems, service bonding, separately derived systems, equipment grounding conductors, bonding jumpers, raceway bonding, parallel paths, objectionable current, metal piping, structural metal, and effective ground-fault current paths. Special-system preparation may involve emergency systems, legally required standby systems, optional standby systems, fire pumps, generators, healthcare facilities, hazardous locations, marinas, swimming pools, photovoltaic systems, energy storage systems, electric vehicle charging equipment, and communications systems. Candidates should practice connecting plan information with the applicable NEC requirements. Business and law questions may involve contracts, estimating, bidding, project scheduling, financial controls, employment practices, insurance, safety programs, recordkeeping, permits, inspections, license use, supervision, and the responsibilities of a listed qualified individual. Open Book Test The North Carolina Unlimited Electrical Contractor examination is an open-book test. Candidates may use the 2020 National Electrical Code and NFPA 72, National Fire Alarm and Signaling Code, 2019 Edition, as the technical exam-room references included in this package. Submit the required personal, employment, experience, and background information to the Board. Provide character references. Include the written character statements required with the application. Submit experience verification. Provide records and statements documenting qualifying electrical experience. Submit the examination fee. Include the applicable payment with the completed application. Receive Board approval. The Board reviews the application and determines whether the applicant meets the Unlimited examination requirements. Receive examination authorization. Approved candidates receive eligibility and scheduling instructions. Schedule the examination. Register with PSI and select an appointment within the authorized testing period. Prepare the approved references. Confirm that the 2020 NEC and NFPA 72, 2019 Edition, comply with exam-room rules. Complete the examination. Bring the required identification and approved technical references to the testing center. Complete the license application. After passing, submit the licensing information and financial documentation required for the Unlimited classification. Establish a listed qualified individual. The license applicant must list at least one qualified individual who has the authority and responsibility to supervise electrical contracting. Maintain the license. Follow renewal, continuing education, financial responsibility, supervision, and compliance requirements. State Requirements The North Carolina State Board of Examiners of Electrical Contractors regulates the Unlimited examination and license. The Board establishes applicant qualifications, approves examinations, certifies qualified individuals, issues licenses, and enforces electrical contracting laws and rules. An applicant for the Unlimited classification must document at least 9,000 hours of qualifying experience. At least 8,000 hours must be primary experience. The remaining experience may be primary, secondary, or a combination of both. Primary experience generally includes direct work installing electrical wiring and equipment governed by the NEC or work activities directly related to those installations. Credit may also be available for qualifying supervisory, estimating, inspection, engineering, instructional, maintenance, military, and other approved electrical experience. The Unlimited applicant must submit written statements from at least two people who are familiar with the applicant’s electrical experience and can attest to the applicant’s ability to supervise and direct all electrical wiring or installation work performed by an Unlimited electrical contracting business. The Unlimited license permits a license holder to engage in electrical contracting projects regardless of project value. Unlike the Limited and Intermediate classifications, the Unlimited classification does not impose a maximum dollar value on a single electrical contracting project. The broad project authority of the Unlimited license does not remove the requirement to comply with the National Electrical Code, state building codes, permits, inspections, contract obligations, occupational safety requirements, and other laws governing the work. Electrical contracting must be conducted in the exact name shown on the active license. Each principal and branch place of business must comply with the Board’s licensing and listed qualified individual requirements. A listed qualified individual must be regularly on active duty and have the authority and responsibility to supervise and direct electrical contracting performed under the license. Applicants for an Unlimited license must provide the financial responsibility or bonding ability documentation required for the classification. The information must be submitted in the name of the license applicant and accepted by the Board. Passing the examination certifies the individual’s qualifications but does not by itself authorize electrical contracting. The appropriate license must be issued and active before the person or business offers to perform or performs regulated electrical contracting work. License holders must remain within the law even though the Unlimited classification has no project-value ceiling. Fraud, misrepresentation, unlicensed contracting, misuse of a license, false advertising, gross negligence, and other prohibited conduct may result in disciplinary action. Unlimited electrical work may involve large services, switchboards, panelboards, transformers, motor systems, generators, emergency power, fire alarm systems, special occupancies, hazardous locations, renewable energy equipment, and extensive electrical plans. Effective preparation requires familiarity with multiple NEC articles and the ability to apply several requirements to the same installation. The North Carolina Unlimited Electrical Contractor examination is open book for the approved technical references. Candidates may use the 2020 NEC and NFPA 72, 2019 Edition, during the examination. The licensing law, Board rules, and NASCLA business reference are included for closed-book preparation and cannot be consulted during the test. Exam Details The North Carolina Unlimited Electrical Contractor examination contains 100 multiple-choice questions. Candidates have a maximum of six hours to complete the examination, and a minimum score of 70 percent is required to pass. The examination is administered after the North Carolina State Board of Examiners of Electrical Contractors approves the applicant. Candidates must receive examination authorization before scheduling a testing appointment. The examination evaluates technical, regulatory, supervisory, and business knowledge needed to direct electrical contracting without a project-value limitation. Questions may involve the National Electrical Code, NFPA 72, electrical plans, specifications, calculations, permits, inspections, licensing law, Board rules, estimating, and business practices. Service and feeder preparation may include load calculations, service conductor sizing, service equipment, disconnecting means, grounding electrode conductors, grounded conductors, parallel conductors, transformer secondaries, feeder demand factors, voltage drop, and protection of conductors and equipment. Branch-circuit preparation should include conductor ampacity, continuous loads, receptacle and lighting loads, appliance circuits, multiwire branch circuits, overcurrent protection, conductor identification, voltage limitations, and requirements for particular occupancies or equipment. Motor questions may involve full-load current, branch-circuit conductor sizing, feeder sizing, overload protection, short-circuit and ground-fault protection, controllers, disconnecting means, duty ratings, multimotor installations, and the proper use of NEC motor tables. Transformer preparation may include primary and secondary conductor sizing, overcurrent protection, grounding and bonding, separately derived systems, transformer vaults, ventilation, clearances, installations in buildings, and secondary-system calculations. Grounding and bonding questions may involve grounding electrode systems, service bonding, separately derived systems, equipment grounding conductors, bonding jumpers, raceway bonding, objectionable current, metal piping, structural metal, and effective ground-fault current paths. Raceway and conductor questions may address conduit fill, conductor adjustment, ambient-temperature correction, terminal limitations, conductor insulation, support, bends, wet locations, physical protection, cable trays, underground installations, pull boxes, junction boxes, and conductor-pulling requirements. Overcurrent-protection preparation should include standard fuse and circuit-breaker ratings, conductor protection, tap conductors, transformer protection, motor circuits, selective coordination, series ratings, interrupting ratings, equipment protection, and permitted exceptions. Special-system preparation may involve emergency systems, legally required standby systems, optional standby systems, fire pumps, generators, healthcare facilities, hazardous locations, marinas, swimming pools, photovoltaic systems, energy storage systems, and electric vehicle charging equipment. Fire alarm preparation may include control units, initiating devices, notification appliances, supervising stations, emergency communications, signaling line circuits, notification appliance circuits, power supplies, batteries, inspection, testing, maintenance, and documentation. Electrical plans may require candidates to interpret symbols, riser diagrams, panel schedules, feeder routes, motor connections, lighting layouts, conductor sizes, equipment ratings, and project notes. Candidates should practice connecting information shown on plans with the applicable NEC requirements. Business and law questions may involve contracts, estimating, bidding, scheduling, financial controls, employment practices, insurance, safety programs, recordkeeping, permits, inspections, license use, supervision, and the responsibilities of a listed qualified individual. Open Book Test The North Carolina Unlimited Electrical Contractor examination is an open-book test. Candidates may use the 2020 National Electrical Code and NFPA 72, National Fire Alarm and Signaling Code, 2019 Edition, as the technical exam-room references included in this package. The highlighted and tabbed 2020 NEC supports questions involving services, feeders, branch circuits, motors, transformers, generators, grounding, bonding, conductor sizing, raceways, overcurrent protection, emergency systems, special occupancies, and special equipment. The highlighted and tabbed NFPA 72, 2019 Edition, supports questions involving fire alarm fundamentals, initiating devices, notification appliances, supervising stations, emergency communications, pathways, power supplies, inspection, testing, maintenance, and documentation. Temporary tabs, removable notes, divider tabs, stapled inserts, loose pages, and unauthorized added materials are not allowed. Open-book testing still requires advanced familiarity with both technical references. Candidates should know how to move from a question to the proper article, chapter, table, definition, exception, annex, or cross-reference without searching randomly. A motor-feeder question may require several NEC sections and tables. A transformer question may involve primary protection, secondary conductors, grounding, bonding, and separately derived system requirements. A fire alarm question may require both the NEC and NFPA 72. Candidates should practice identifying which reference controls the subject before beginning a search. Installation and conductor questions will generally require the NEC, while system-performance, notification, inspection, testing, and maintenance questions may require NFPA 72. Timed reference practice is essential for a six-hour, 100-question examination. Candidates should develop a repeatable process: identify the topic, choose the correct reference, locate the governing provision, read the complete rule, check exceptions, and complete the required calculation or interpretation. Licensing Steps Confirm the Unlimited classification. Review the authority and responsibilities associated with an electrical license that has no project-value limitation. Document qualifying experience. Gather employment and project records showing the required primary, secondary, or equivalent electrical experience. Prepare supervisory statements. Obtain written statements from people familiar with the applicant’s ability to supervise and direct electrical wiring and installation work. Complete the examination application. Submit the required personal, employment, experience, and background information to the Board. Provide required supporting statements. Include character references, supervisory statements, experience verification, and other requested documentation. Submit the examination fee. Include the applicable payment with the completed application. Receive Board approval. The Board reviews the application and determines whether the applicant meets the Unlimited examination qualifications. Receive examination authorization. Approved candidates receive eligibility and scheduling instructions. Schedule the examination. Register with the testing provider and select an appointment within the authorized testing period. Prepare the approved references. Confirm that the highlighted and tabbed 2020 NEC and NFPA 72, 2019 Edition, comply with exam-room rules. Complete the examination. Bring the required identification and approved technical references to the testing center. Complete the license application. After passing, submit the licensing information and financial documentation required for the Unlimited classification. Establish a listed qualified individual. The license applicant must list a qualified individual with authority and responsibility to supervise electrical contracting. Maintain the license. Follow current renewal, continuing education, financial responsibility, supervision, and compliance requirements. State Requirements The North Carolina State Board of Examiners of Electrical Contractors regulates the Unlimited examination and license. The Board establishes applicant qualifications, authorizes examinations, certifies qualified individuals, issues licenses, and enforces electrical contracting laws and rules. An applicant for the Unlimited classification must document at least 9,000 hours of qualifying experience. At least 8,000 hours must be primary experience. The remaining experience may consist of primary experience, secondary experience, or a combination of both. Primary experience generally includes direct work installing electrical wiring and equipment governed by the NEC or work activities directly related to those installations. Credit may also be available for qualifying supervisory, estimating, inspection, engineering, instructional, maintenance, military, and other recognized electrical experience. The Unlimited applicant must provide statements from people familiar with the applicant’s electrical work and ability to supervise and direct electrical installations performed by an Unlimited electrical contracting business. The Unlimited license permits electrical contracting projects regardless of project value. Unlike the Limited and Intermediate classifications, the Unlimited classification does not impose a maximum dollar value on a single electrical contracting project. The absence of a project-value limit does not remove the requirement to comply with the National Electrical Code, state building codes, permits, inspections, contract obligations, workplace safety rules, and other laws governing electrical work. Electrical contracting must be conducted in the exact name shown on the active license. Each principal or branch place of business must comply with the Board’s licensing and listed qualified individual requirements. A listed qualified individual must be regularly on active duty and have the authority and responsibility to supervise and direct the electrical contracting performed under the license. Applicants for an Unlimited license must provide the financial responsibility or bonding documentation required for the classification. The information must be submitted in the name of the license applicant and accepted as part of the licensing process. Passing the examination establishes the individual’s examination qualification but does not independently authorize electrical contracting. The proper license must be issued and active before the individual or business offers to perform or performs regulated work. License holders must continue to comply with applicable laws even though the Unlimited classification has no project-value ceiling. Fraud, misrepresentation, misuse of a license, false advertising, gross negligence, and unlicensed contracting may result in disciplinary action. Reinforcing-bar references support review of bar identification, placement, spacing, supports, ties, bends, splices, and general reinforcement practices. Formwork study focuses on the temporary systems used to shape and support concrete until it can carry the necessary loads. Welding preparation addresses terminology, equipment, processes, joints, positions, symbols, materials, and safety. Excavation and OSHA references support questions involving trenches, protective systems, access, inspections, equipment hazards, personal protective equipment, fall protection, scaffolding, electrical safety, and other construction-site responsibilities. The business and law portion of preparation should not be overlooked. Contractors are expected to understand project administration, contracts, estimating, financial management, licensing responsibilities, employment considerations, risk management, and the legal obligations involved in operating a construction business in North Carolina. Open Book Test The North Carolina Billboard & Sign Contractor exam is an open-book examination. Open-book testing allows candidates to use approved references, but it still requires careful preparation. The available testing time is not intended for reading each publication from the beginning or searching randomly through unfamiliar chapters. A productive study method is to assign each reference a clear purpose. Use the concrete book for questions involving concrete ingredients, mixture proportioning, production, placement, curing, and performance. Use the reinforcing reference for bar placement and detailing topics. Use the formwork book for temporary support systems, loads, construction practices, and related safety considerations. Use the welding text for welding processes, equipment, joints, positions, terminology, and safe procedures. The North Carolina excavation guide should be familiar whenever a question involves digging, trench conditions, underground hazards, soil, protective systems, or excavation operations. The OSHA construction standards should be used for federal jobsite-safety requirements. The North Carolina business and law guide should be the primary reference for contractor administration, business practices, project management, and state-specific responsibilities. Before test day, review each table of contents, index, chapter layout, glossary, appendix, and major heading. Practice turning a question into two or three search terms. For example, a question about trench access may direct you toward excavation requirements, ladders, or means of egress. A question about a reinforcing-bar connection may require searching for splices, development, tying, or placement. Tabs, highlights, and notes should be prepared only in accordance with the current testing rules. Candidates should review the PSI Candidate Information Bulletin and their eligibility instructions for the most current policies governing approved references and materials at the testing center. Licensing Steps Select the appropriate classification and limitation. North Carolina contractor licenses are organized by classification and limitation. The classification identifies the type of work the license covers, while the limitation determines the permitted financial size of individual projects. Prepare the legal applicant information. The application should be submitted in the name of the individual or business entity that will bid, contract, and operate. A license is issued to a specific legal entity and applies only to work performed by that entity. Complete the North Carolina license application. New license applications are submitted through the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors. Meet the Board’s application requirements. Applicants must satisfy the requirements associated with age, character, financial qualification, classification, limitation, and supporting documentation. Designate a qualifier. The qualifier is the responsible managing employee, owner, officer, or qualifying member who completes the examination required for the classification. Receive examination eligibility. After the application is reviewed and found eligible, the Board provides the information needed to schedule the examination with PSI. Schedule and complete the required examination. Candidates should follow the scheduling, identification, testing-center, reference-material, and security instructions issued for their examination. Complete the Board approval process. Passing an examination does not by itself create a contractor license. The application and all required information remain subject to review and approval by the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors. State Requirements North Carolina requires a general contractor license when a contractor undertakes work that meets the licensing threshold established by state law. The North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors regulates license classifications, limitations, qualifiers, examinations, applications, and renewals. Applicants must be at least 18 years old, demonstrate good moral character, meet the financial requirement for the selected license limitation, complete the required application, and successfully satisfy the examination requirement for the desired classification. The applicant may be an individual or a business entity, but the name on the license must match the entity that will perform and contract for the work. North Carolina licenses use three principal limitations: limited, intermediate, and unlimited. The limitation affects the maximum value of an individual project the licensee may undertake and carries its own financial qualification requirements. Candidates should select the limitation that fits their intended operations and submit the financial documentation required by the Board. A qualifier holds the examination credential used to qualify a license. Qualifiers may be responsible managing employees, owners, officers, or qualifying members of an eligible business organization. The qualifier and the licensee are not automatically the same. The license belongs to the approved legal entity, while the qualifying credential belongs to the individual who satisfies the examination requirement. Applicants should carefully review current Board statutes, rules, application instructions, financial standards, and entity requirements before filing. Business registrations, annual reports, tax standing, and other entity records should remain current when applicable. Examination eligibility, application approval, and final license issuance are controlled by the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors. Reference Books Contractor’s Guide to Business, Law and Project Management – North Carolina General Contractors Edition, 10th EditionThis North Carolina-focused contractor reference covers business organization, licensing responsibilities, contract administration, estimating, project management, financial practices, employment matters, risk management, and other subjects relevant to operating a contracting business. North Carolina Excavation Safety Guidelines, 2022 or LaterThis state-specific safety publication supports review of excavation and trenching hazards, protective measures, safe work practices, underground utility considerations, access, inspections, and responsibilities affecting excavation operations. Design and Control of Concrete Mixtures – Steven H. Kosmatka & William C. Panarese, 17th Edition (2021)A detailed concrete reference covering cementitious materials, aggregates, water, admixtures, mixture proportioning, production, placement, curing, durability, testing, and concrete-performance considerations. Placing Reinforcing BarsA practical reference for reinforcing-steel work, including bar identification, fabrication, handling, placement, supports, tying, spacing, splices, and reinforcement practices used in concrete construction. SP-4 Formwork for Concrete, 8th Edition (2014)This formwork reference addresses materials, design considerations, loads, construction methods, shores, reshoring, wall and column forms, slab systems, and safe practices for temporary concrete-support structures. Modern Welding, 12th Edition (2020)A comprehensive welding textbook covering welding processes, equipment, power sources, metals, joints, positions, symbols, cutting methods, inspection concepts, and safe shop and field practices. Code of Federal Regulations – 29 CFR Part 1926 (OSHA Construction Standards)The federal construction-safety standards address workplace requirements involving personal protective equipment, fall protection, scaffolds, ladders, electrical hazards, material handling, tools, welding, excavation, concrete construction, steel erection, and additional construction activities. Test Information and Study Materials Begin by inventorying the books and matching each one to the major subject areas. Create a weekly study plan that alternates technical reading with reference-navigation exercises. A study session may include reading a concrete chapter, reviewing major terms, and then answering several questions that require locating specific facts in the text. Do not rely only on memorization. The exam may require candidates to distinguish between similar terms, identify the correct standard, interpret a practical situation, or choose the appropriate procedure. Understanding the subject helps determine which book to open, while navigation practice helps locate the supporting information efficiently. Spend additional time on indexes and terminology. Technical questions often use wording that differs from the exact heading in a book. A reference may organize information under reinforcement rather than rebar, protective systems rather than trench boxes, or form pressure rather than wall forms. Building a stronger vocabulary improves both comprehension and search speed. Practice mixed-topic sessions as the examination approaches. Move between business law, concrete, reinforcement, welding, excavation, formwork, and OSHA questions instead of studying only one subject for long periods. This better reflects the mental task of identifying which reference applies to each question. On test day, read every question carefully, identify the central subject, eliminate clearly incorrect choices, and then confirm the answer in the appropriate book. Avoid spending too much time on a single difficult item. A structured approach helps preserve time for questions that can be answered more efficiently. How 1 Exam Prep Helps You Reach Your Goal 1 Exam Prep helps contractor candidates build a more organized path toward exam readiness. This North Carolina Billboard & Sign Contractor Exam Book Package gathers the listed references into one focused collection, reducing the need to search for each publication separately. Our approach emphasizes practical preparation. Candidates benefit from understanding the trade concepts, recognizing the language used in the references, and developing a repeatable process for open-book navigation. Organized study guidance can help you divide a broad exam outline into manageable topics and maintain steady progress. Trade-focused review encourages candidates to connect the books rather than treat them as unrelated publications. Concrete foundations involve mixture design, reinforcement, formwork, excavation, and safety. Steel sign structures may involve welding procedures, material handling, access equipment, and OSHA requirements. Business and project-management knowledge supports the administrative side of planning and completing the work. Reference-navigation practice is equally important. Learning where information is located, how indexes are written, and which search terms lead to the correct section can improve confidence during an open-book examination. A prepared candidate enters the testing center with a clear understanding of what each reference covers and how to use it. 1 Exam Prep supports a realistic, confidence-building study structure without promising a particular examination or licensing outcome. Preparation, application eligibility, exam performance, and final licensing decisions remain the responsibility of the candidate and the appropriate licensing authorities. Frequently Asked Questions What books are included in the North Carolina Billboard & Sign Contractor Exam Book Package? The package includes the North Carolina contractor business and law guide, North Carolina Excavation Safety Guidelines, Design and Control of Concrete Mixtures, Placing Reinforcing Bars, SP-4 Formwork for Concrete, Modern Welding, and 29 CFR Part 1926 OSHA Construction Standards. Is the North Carolina Billboard & Sign Contractor exam open book? Yes. The examination is open book. Candidates should become familiar with the organization, indexes, chapters, and terminology of the approved references before test day. Does this package include both trade and business references? Yes. The package contains technical books for concrete, reinforcing steel, formwork, welding, excavation, and construction safety, along with the North Carolina contractor guide for business, law, and project management. Who administers the North Carolina contractor examinations? Computer-based examinations for the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors are administered by PSI Examination Services. Candidates receive scheduling eligibility after completing the applicable Board process. Do I apply for the examination before applying for the contractor license? Applicants generally submit the new license application to the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors. After the application is reviewed and the candidate is found eligible, examination-scheduling information is issued. Does passing the exam automatically issue a North Carolina contractor license? No. Passing the required examination is one part of the licensing process. The applicant must also satisfy the Board’s application, financial, entity, character, classification, limitation, and approval requirements. How should I study for an open-book contractor exam? Study the underlying concepts, learn the purpose of every reference, review each index and table of contents, practice searching by keywords, and complete timed navigation exercises. Open-book preparation should focus on both knowledge and efficient reference use. Are the books useful after the examination? Yes. The publications cover contractor business practices, concrete construction, reinforcing steel, formwork, welding, excavation safety, and OSHA requirements that can remain useful as professional reference materials. Can this package guarantee that I will pass the exam? No book package can guarantee an examination result. Performance depends on the candidate’s preparation, familiarity with the references, understanding of the subject matter, and ability to apply that knowledge during the examination.

description: North Carolina Boring and Tunneling Contractor Exam Book Package Prepare for the North Carolina S(Boring and Tunneling) Contractor examination with a focused exam book package built around the references permitted in the examination center. The North Carolina S(Boring and Tunneling) classification covers the construction of underground or underwater passageways by digging or boring through and under the earth's surface. The scope includes bracing and compacting passageways so they are safe for their intended purpose and preparing ground surfaces at points of ingress and egress. Candidates pursuing this specialty should be prepared for questions involving underground construction methods, sitework, concrete, reinforcement, safety, rigging, excavation-related requirements, and contractor regulations. The examination is open book, but an important distinction applies: only certain references from the overall examination reference list are permitted inside the testing center. For the S(Boring and Tunneling) exam, the approved exam-room references are North Carolina Occupational Safety and Health Standards for the Construction Industry, with latest available amendments and Handbook of Rigging, 5th Edition, 2009. Other references associated with the examination are not permitted inside the exam room. Candidates should therefore develop a two-part preparation strategy. First, become highly familiar with the two books that can be used during the test. Second, study the major concepts represented by the non-permitted references before exam day so those subjects can be approached from knowledge rather than depending on a book lookup. This North Carolina Boring and Tunneling Contractor Exam Book Package gives candidates the approved books they can actively navigate during the examination. Handbook of Rigging, 5th Edition, 2009A technical rigging reference covering lifting and rigging principles, wire rope, slings, chains, hardware, load handling, inspection, rigging practices, and other concepts associated with safe hoisting operations. Exam Details The North Carolina S(Boring and Tunneling) Contractor examination is administered through PSI for candidates approved through the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors. The examination contains 60 questions. Candidates are allowed 120 minutes to complete the exam, and a score of 70% is required to pass. The current examination content outline includes: Boring and Tunneling: 22 questions Sitework: 6 questions Concrete: 10 questions Concrete Reinforcement: 5 questions Hoisting and Rigging: 5 questions Safety: 5 questions One Call: 2 questions Erosion and Sedimentation Control: 2 questions Liens: 1 question Laws and Regulations: 2 questions Boring and Tunneling is the largest individual examination category, with 22 questions. Candidates should devote substantial preparation time to underground passageway construction, boring and tunneling methods, excavation-related operations, ground preparation, support considerations, and the practical construction knowledge associated with this specialty. Concrete and concrete reinforcement together also account for a significant portion of the exam. Study should include the construction concepts represented by these subjects even though several of the technical references associated with them are not allowed inside the examination center. Safety and Hoisting and Rigging account for five questions each. These are particularly important areas for reference navigation because the two books included in this package are approved for exam-room use and directly support preparation for these subjects. Open Book Test The North Carolina S(Boring and Tunneling) Contractor examination is an open-book test. Candidates may bring approved reference materials into the examination center, but only the references specifically authorized for the exam may be used. The two approved references are North Carolina Occupational Safety and Health Standards for the Construction Industry, with latest available amendments and Handbook of Rigging, 5th Edition, 2009. Because the exam contains 60 questions and allows 120 minutes, candidates have an average of approximately two minutes per question. Effective open-book testing therefore requires more than having the correct books on the desk. Candidates should know where important information is located and be able to move quickly between relevant sections. PSI permits approved references to be highlighted, underlined, and indexed before the examination session. Permanent tabs may be used. Removable tabs are not permitted, and notes may not be written on tabs. References may not be written in before or during the examination session. Candidates should use permanent indexing strategically. Instead of marking every possible page, organize references around major subjects that are likely to support exam questions. For the safety standards, useful navigation areas may include excavation, underground construction, personal protective equipment, material handling, access and egress, equipment, and other construction safety topics. For the rigging handbook, candidates should become comfortable locating sling information, wire rope, hardware, load-handling principles, inspections, and common rigging practices. Licensing Steps Review the North Carolina S(Boring and Tunneling) classification. Understand the scope of underground and underwater passageway work covered by the specialty. Submit the applicable licensing or examination request materials. Examination eligibility is determined through the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors. Identify the qualifying individual. The qualifying individual is the person who meets the examination requirement associated with the classification sought by the license applicant. Receive examination eligibility. After approval, eligible candidates receive examination scheduling instructions. Schedule the examination through PSI. The approved candidate follows the examination registration and scheduling process. Prepare for all examination subject areas. Study boring and tunneling, sitework, concrete, reinforcement, rigging, safety, One Call, erosion and sedimentation control, liens, and laws and regulations. Prepare the approved exam-room references. Become familiar with the safety standards and rigging handbook and organize them according to current testing rules. Complete the examination. Take the North Carolina S(Boring and Tunneling) Contractor exam and continue through the applicable licensing process. Examination eligibility is determined by the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors. Candidates should complete the applicable Board process before attempting to schedule the specialty examination. State Requirements The North Carolina S(Boring and Tunneling) specialty classification covers the construction of underground or underwater passageways by digging or boring through and under the earth's surface. The classification includes bracing and compacting those passageways so they are safe for their intended purpose. The scope also includes preparation of ground surfaces at points of ingress and egress. This makes site preparation, underground construction practices, ground conditions, excavation, access, support, and construction safety important knowledge areas for candidates entering the specialty. North Carolina contractor licensing uses qualifying individuals whose examinations establish qualification for applicable classifications. The license applicant must follow the requirements established by the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors for the requested classification and license limitation. The S(Boring and Tunneling) specialty is also included within the scope of certain broader North Carolina contractor classifications. Candidates seeking the specialty directly should prepare specifically for the S(Boring and Tunneling) examination content and follow the Board's licensing procedures applicable to their circumstances. Reference Books North Carolina Occupational Safety and Health Standards for the Construction Industry, with latest available amendmentsThis approved exam-room reference supports study of construction safety requirements and workplace protection. For a boring and tunneling candidate, familiarity with excavation and underground construction safety, protective equipment, equipment operation, access, material handling, and related jobsite requirements can be especially useful. Handbook of Rigging, 5th Edition, 2009This approved exam-room reference supports study of hoisting and rigging. Candidates can use it to strengthen knowledge of lifting equipment, slings, wire rope, chains, rigging hardware, hitches, load considerations, inspection, and safe rigging practices. Exam Room Approved Books The following books are allowed into the North Carolina S(Boring and Tunneling) examination room: North Carolina Occupational Safety and Health Standards for the Construction Industry, with latest available amendmentsApproved for exam-room use and particularly useful for the Safety portion of the examination and construction safety questions associated with underground work. Handbook of Rigging, 5th Edition, 2009Approved for exam-room use and particularly useful for the Hoisting and Rigging portion of the examination. Candidates are responsible for bringing their approved reference materials to the examination center. Preparing directly with these books before test day helps develop familiarity with their structure and improves the ability to recognize where an answer may be located. Test Information and Study Materials Several references associated with preparation for the North Carolina Boring and Tunneling Contractor examination are not allowed in the exam room. These materials represent subject matter that candidates should study before test day rather than expecting to use the books during the examination. The books and materials identified as not allowed in the exam include: North Carolina Administrative Code, Title 15A, Chapter 4 Sedimentation Control, including the latest amendmentsSupports preparation involving erosion and sedimentation control requirements. North Carolina General Statutes Chapter 113A, Article 4 Sedimentation Pollution Control Act of 1973Supports study of North Carolina sedimentation pollution control requirements associated with land-disturbing activities. North Carolina Excavation Safety Guidelines, 2022 or laterSupports preparation involving underground facilities, excavation planning, One Call concepts, and excavation safety responsibilities. Contractor’s Guide to Business, Law and Project Management - North Carolina General Contractors Edition, 10th EditionSupports review of contractor business, law, project management, and regulatory concepts. Pipe and Excavation ContractingA trade-oriented reference useful for studying excavation, underground construction, piping, equipment, and related field practices. Laws and Regulations Applicable to General Contracting in the State of North CarolinaSupports preparation involving North Carolina contractor laws and regulatory requirements. Jacked Tunnel Design and Construction, 1999A technical study reference addressing jacked tunnel design and construction concepts. Standard Construction Guidelines for Microtunneling, 2001Supports technical preparation involving microtunneling methods and underground construction practices. Code of Practice for Tunnels Under Construction, 2006A study resource associated with tunnel construction practices and safety considerations. Design and Control of Concrete Mixtures, 17th EditionSupports preparation for concrete materials, mixture fundamentals, placement considerations, and concrete construction concepts. Training and Certification of Field Personnel for Unbonded Post-Tensioning - Level 1 Field FundamentalsSupports study of field concepts associated with unbonded post-tensioning and concrete reinforcement. Placing Reinforcing BarsA technical study reference covering reinforcing steel placement and related concrete reinforcement practices. Since these books are not available for consultation during the examination, advance preparation is especially important. Candidates should develop a working understanding of the technical ideas represented by each major subject rather than relying on last-minute reference searching. Candidates should understand concrete fundamentals, placement concepts, reinforcement principles, reinforcing bars, and construction practices represented by the listed study references. For Hoisting and Rigging, use the included Handbook of Rigging actively. Practice locating information involving slings, wire rope, chains, hardware, hitches, equipment limitations, inspections, and load-handling principles. The objective is not simply to memorize page numbers but to understand the organization of the book well enough to locate information efficiently. For Safety, become familiar with the structure of the North Carolina construction safety standards. Underground work can involve excavation hazards, equipment, restricted access, falling or moving materials, lifting operations, protective equipment, and other conditions requiring careful safety planning. One Call, erosion and sedimentation control, liens, and laws and regulations account for fewer questions individually, but together they can still affect the final score. Use the approved books for repeated open-book navigation practice, and use the non-permitted materials to build knowledge of topics that will need to be understood without having those references available in the exam room. Repetition builds familiarity with terminology and reference organization. Reference navigation is especially useful for the safety and rigging portions of this examination. Knowing how the two approved books are arranged can reduce unnecessary searching and help candidates manage the 120-minute testing period more effectively. 1 Exam Prep helps candidates create a clearer path from initial study through exam-day preparation by combining trade knowledge, organized review, reference familiarity, and practice. The objective is to help candidates approach the North Carolina Boring and Tunneling Contractor exam with a stronger study structure and greater confidence in using the materials available to them. State Requirements North Carolina contractor licensing is organized by classification and limitation. The classification relates to the type of construction work performed, while the limitation relates to the level of projects the contractor is authorized to undertake. The applying entity must designate a qualifier who satisfies the examination requirement. The qualifier completes the required exam, while the license is issued to the approved applicant or business entity after all applicable requirements have been met. Concrete construction contractors may be responsible for foundations, slabs, walls, structural members, reinforced concrete, formwork, placement, curing, cutting, repair, and related construction activities. The exact scope of work should remain within the authority of the issued classification and limitation. Concrete projects may require compliance with structural requirements, building codes, occupational safety standards, approved plans, inspection procedures, permit requirements, and administrative policies. Contractors should understand that compliance extends through the entire project, from planning and formwork through placement, curing, cutting, inspection, and closeout. Safety is a continuing responsibility. Concrete work can involve reinforcing steel, formwork systems, heavy equipment, lifting operations, elevated work, scaffolds, ladders, cutting equipment, electrical exposure, pumps, trucks, and material handling. Contractors should plan and supervise work with these hazards in mind. Concrete contractors may also need to coordinate with owners, engineers, architects, inspectors, general contractors, subcontractors, suppliers, testing agencies, and workers. Project documentation, contracts, schedules, quality requirements, and safety procedures should be managed throughout the work. A contractor license does not replace other legal or business obligations. Business registration, taxes, insurance, workers’ compensation, permits, inspections, contracts, employment responsibilities, and local requirements may apply separately. Reference Books North Carolina Occupational Safety and Health Standards for the Construction Industry, with Latest Available AmendmentsThis highlighted and tabbed exam-room reference contains occupational safety and health requirements applicable to construction work in North Carolina. It supports review of employer responsibilities, worker protection, fall hazards, scaffolds, ladders, tools, material handling, excavation, electrical exposure, and concrete construction safety. North Carolina Building Code: Building Code 2018This highlighted and tabbed exam-room reference contains building-code provisions applicable to construction in North Carolina. It supports study of building requirements, structural provisions, materials, inspections, referenced standards, and code compliance. North Carolina Administrative Code and Policies, 2018 EditionThis highlighted and tabbed exam-room reference supports review of code administration, permits, inspections, approvals, responsibilities, enforcement, and related construction policies. SP-4 Formwork for Concrete, 2014, 8th EditionThis study-only reference covers formwork systems, materials, loads, bracing, shoring, reshoring, construction, removal, safety, and field practices. Design and Control of Concrete Mixtures, 17th EditionThis study-only reference explains concrete materials, mixture proportioning, production, testing, placement, curing, strength, durability, and quality control. Sawcutting Joints in Concrete, Bruce A. Suprenant, 1995This study-only publication addresses concrete joint planning, cutting timing, equipment, procedures, and crack-control considerations. Sawcutting Concrete Flatwork, Rosalie Johnston, 1994This study-only publication focuses on sawcutting practices for concrete flatwork, including joint layout, timing, equipment, and field procedures. Taking the Tedium Out of Cutting, 1981This study-only reference provides practical information related to concrete cutting methods, equipment use, planning, and field efficiency. Tips for Cutting Concrete, 1987This study-only publication provides practical guidance on concrete cutting procedures, equipment, safety, timing, and jobsite considerations. Erectors' Manual – Standards and Guidelines for the Erection of PreCast Concrete Products, 2nd Edition, 1999This study-only manual addresses planning, lifting, handling, bracing, alignment, placement, and safe erection of precast concrete products. Contractor’s Guide to Business, Law and Project Management – North Carolina General Contractors Edition, 10th EditionThis study-only reference covers business organization, financial management, estimating, contracts, project administration, employment practices, insurance, risk management, and North Carolina contractor law. Laws and Regulations Applicable to General Contracting in the State of North CarolinaThis study-only reference supports review of North Carolina contractor licensing laws, legal obligations, regulatory responsibilities, and compliance requirements. Placing Reinforcing BarsThis study-only reference covers reinforcing-bar placement, supports, ties, spacing, bends, laps, detailing, and coordination with formwork and concrete placement. Exam Room Approved Books North Carolina Occupational Safety and Health Standards for the Construction Industry, with Latest Available AmendmentsThis highlighted and tabbed safety reference is allowed inside the North Carolina Concrete Construction Contractor Exam. North Carolina Building Code: Building Code 2018This highlighted and tabbed building-code reference is allowed inside the examination room. ACI 318-14: Building Code Requirements for Structural Concrete and CommentaryThis highlighted and tabbed structural concrete code and commentary is allowed inside the examination room. North Carolina Administrative Code and Policies, 2018 EditionThis highlighted and tabbed administrative reference is allowed inside the examination room. The formwork, concrete mixture, sawcutting, precast erection, business, legal, and reinforcing-bar books included in the package are study-only references and are not identified as allowed inside the exam. Test Information and Study Materials Begin by separating the four exam-room references from the study-only books. Learn the purpose of each approved reference and practice identifying which book applies to a question before searching for the answer. Study the North Carolina Building Code and ACI 318-14 together when reviewing structural concrete topics. Use the commentary in ACI 318-14 to improve understanding while recognizing the difference between mandatory code provisions and explanatory material. Use SP-4 Formwork for Concrete and Placing Reinforcing Bars to build practical knowledge of form systems, shoring, bracing, reinforcement placement, spacing, supports, ties, and coordination before concrete placement. Review Design and Control of Concrete Mixtures for concrete ingredients, mixture proportioning, production, testing, placement, curing, durability, and quality. Connect these subjects to the structural and building-code requirements found in the approved references. Study the four sawcutting publications together. Focus on joint purpose, cutting timing, layout, equipment, procedures, flatwork, crack control, and safety. Use the Erectors’ Manual to review lifting, handling, bracing, sequencing, placement, and safety for precast concrete products. Connect those practices to the occupational safety standards. Complete timed practice using only the four exam-room books. Use the study-only references before and after each practice session to strengthen technical subjects and correct misunderstandings. Please allow an additional 15 business days on highlighted and tabbed trade book package orders. How 1 Exam Prep Helps You Reach Your Goal 1 Exam Prep helps concrete contractor candidates organize a large reference list into a practical study system. Organized study guidance can help candidates divide the material into manageable sections, track progress, and identify topics that require additional review. This reduces the risk of concentrating only on familiar subjects while overlooking code, safety, or business content. Practice-oriented preparation helps candidates build both knowledge and reference-navigation skills. Reference navigation is especially important for the four books allowed inside the exam. Familiarity with chapters, indexes, section numbers, tables, commentary, and administrative provisions can help candidates use their testing time more effectively. No book package can guarantee passing, licensing approval, or a specific exam result. Individual performance depends on preparation, experience, understanding, and completion of all applicable licensing requirements. Frequently Asked Questions Which books are allowed inside the North Carolina Concrete Construction Contractor Exam? Does this package include business and law preparation? Yes. It includes the Contractor’s Guide to Business, Law and Project Management and Laws and Regulations Applicable to General Contracting in the State of North Carolina. Does purchasing this package register me for the examination? No. Purchasing the books does not submit a licensing application, create exam eligibility, or schedule a testing appointment. Does passing the exam automatically issue a contractor license? No. Passing the examination is one part of the licensing process. The applicant must satisfy all applicable requirements before a license is issued. Should I confirm the book rules before test day? Yes.
