description: North Carolina Insulation Contractor Exam Online Course Prepare for the North Carolina Insulation Contractor Exam with an organized online course designed for contractors, qualifiers, insulation professionals, and exam candidates pursuing the North Carolina S (Insulation) specialty classification. This course provides a structured way to review important insulation, energy-conservation, and construction-safety concepts while building familiarity with the references approved for the open-book examination. Insulation work plays an important role in building performance, energy efficiency, occupant comfort, moisture management, and code compliance. Contractors working in this specialty must understand more than the installation of insulation products. They may also need working knowledge of thermal performance, building-envelope requirements, jobsite safety, material handling, protective equipment, installation conditions, and the energy provisions that apply to construction projects. The North Carolina Insulation Contractor Exam Online Course helps candidates organize these subjects into manageable study areas. Instead of attempting to study large reference books without direction, students can follow a focused preparation structure that supports subject review, question analysis, and reference navigation. The course is intended to help candidates understand the material and become more efficient at locating relevant information in the approved books. This product includes 6 months of online course access. No physical books are included. Students are responsible for obtaining the correct approved references separately and bringing permitted books to the examination in accordance with current test-center rules. What You Get Online Course Access: 6 months of course access for flexible, self-paced preparation. Insulation-Focused Review: Organized study guidance centered on insulation work, energy conservation, construction safety, and related trade concepts. Open-Book Exam Preparation: Support for learning how to work efficiently with the references permitted in the examination. Practice-Oriented Study Structure: Preparation that encourages topic review, question analysis, and repeated reference lookup. Flexible Learning: Online access that allows students to study around work, family, and project responsibilities. Physical Books: No physical reference books are included with this product. Exam Details The North Carolina Insulation Contractor Exam supports qualification for the S (Insulation) specialty classification. The examination is designed to evaluate knowledge related to insulation work, construction safety, and energy-conservation requirements that affect insulation systems and building-envelope performance. Insulation contractors should be prepared to work with subjects involving thermal resistance, insulation placement, continuity of the thermal envelope, air leakage, material application, installation quality, safety practices, and code-based energy requirements. Candidates may also need to interpret technical language, identify applicable requirements, and determine which reference contains the information needed to answer a question. Exam preparation should combine trade knowledge with reference-navigation skills. Some questions may be answered from knowledge developed through study and field experience. Other questions may require the candidate to locate a specific rule, table, definition, exception, installation requirement, or safety provision in one of the approved books. A productive study plan should include both conceptual review and timed book-lookup practice. Candidates should become familiar with the organization of each reference, including the table of contents, chapter structure, index, definitions, tables, and section numbering. Knowing where information is located is especially important during an open-book exam. Current scheduling instructions, identification requirements, testing policies, and candidate procedures are provided through the North Carolina licensing and examination process. Candidates must follow the instructions issued by the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors and the authorized testing provider. Open Book Test The North Carolina Insulation Contractor Exam is an open-book examination. Candidates may use only the references approved for this specific exam. Open book does not mean that all study materials, manuals, guides, or contractor books may be taken into the testing room. The following two references are approved for use during the examination: North Carolina Occupational Safety and Health Standards for the Construction Industry, with latest available amendments North Carolina Energy Conservation Code, 2018 Edition The approved references should be obtained early in the study process. Candidates who wait until shortly before the examination may not have enough time to learn how each book is organized. Familiarity with the books can make a major difference when a question requires a specific safety standard, energy provision, table, exception, or definition. Students should practice identifying which book is most likely to contain the answer before beginning a search. Questions involving workplace hazards, protective measures, ladders, scaffolds, fall protection, equipment, or construction-site responsibilities are likely to require the occupational safety reference. Questions involving insulation values, energy requirements, thermal-envelope provisions, air leakage, or energy-code compliance are more likely to require the energy conservation code. Reference navigation should be practiced repeatedly. Use the table of contents for broad subject areas, the index for specific terms, and chapter headings or section numbers to confirm the correct provision. When possible, practice under timed conditions so that book lookup becomes part of the study routine rather than an unfamiliar exam-day task. Candidates must also comply with current test-center rules regarding highlights, tabs, handwritten notes, bindings, inserts, and loose papers. Only books that meet the examination provider’s requirements should be brought into the testing room. Licensing Steps Review the classification. Confirm that the North Carolina S (Insulation) specialty classification matches the type of contracting work the applicant intends to perform. Select the appropriate license limitation. North Carolina contractor licenses include a classification and a limitation. The classification determines the type of work, while the limitation controls the value of projects the licensee may undertake. Complete the new license application. The individual or business entity seeking licensure submits an application to the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors. Designate a qualifier. The applicant identifies the individual who will satisfy the examination requirement for the requested classification. Submit supporting information. The application may require business information, ownership details, financial documentation, qualifier information, and other materials associated with the applicant and selected limitation. Receive examination eligibility. Once the application is reviewed and found complete, the approved candidate receives the information needed to schedule the examination. Schedule the exam. Follow the eligibility instructions to arrange the test with the authorized examination provider. Prepare with the approved references. Study insulation, energy-conservation, and safety subjects while practicing efficient book navigation. Take the examination. Follow all identification, scheduling, test-center, and approved-reference requirements. Complete final licensing review. Passing the exam fulfills an examination component, but the license is issued only after the applicant completes the full licensing process and receives approval. The applicant and qualifier are not always the same. The applicant is the person or business entity seeking the license, while the qualifier is the individual whose examination credential supports the requested classification. Passing the exam does not automatically create an active contractor license. State Requirements North Carolina general contractor licensing is administered by the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors. State law requires a general contractor’s license for covered construction work when the total project cost reaches the current statutory licensing threshold. The S (Insulation) classification is a specialty contractor classification. Specialty classifications address construction work requiring particular skills, trades, or crafts. Applicants should make sure the requested classification matches the work they intend to contract, supervise, or perform. A North Carolina license includes both a classification and a limitation. The classification controls the category of construction work. The limitation controls the value of a single project the licensee may undertake. Applicants must satisfy the requirements associated with the limitation they request. The licensing process may include financial qualification, business information, ownership information, supporting documents, and a qualifying examination. The exact application requirements can vary based on the applicant’s legal structure, requested limitation, and qualifier arrangement. The examination requirement is only one part of licensure. A candidate may pass the North Carolina Insulation Contractor Exam and still need to complete additional application requirements before the license is approved and issued. Once licensed, the contractor must work within the approved classification and limitation. Licensees are also responsible for maintaining accurate information with the Board, completing applicable renewal obligations, and complying with North Carolina laws, rules, contracts, safety standards, and construction requirements. Reference Books The following references support preparation for the North Carolina Insulation Contractor Exam. The first two titles are approved for use in the exam room. The remaining titles are study materials and are not allowed during the examination. North Carolina Occupational Safety and Health Standards for the Construction Industry, with latest available amendmentsAn approved exam-room reference covering construction safety requirements, workplace hazards, employee protection, personal protective equipment, fall protection, access, material handling, and other jobsite responsibilities. North Carolina Energy Conservation Code, 2018 EditionAn approved exam-room reference addressing energy-efficiency requirements for buildings, including provisions related to insulation, thermal resistance, building-envelope performance, air leakage, and energy-code compliance. Contractor’s Guide to Business, Law and Project Management – North Carolina General Contractors Edition, 10th EditionA study reference covering contractor business practices, project management, contracts, risk, administration, and North Carolina-specific construction responsibilities. This book is not allowed in the exam room. Insulation Handbook, 2001A study reference covering insulation materials, thermal principles, applications, installation considerations, system performance, and practical insulation concepts. This book is not allowed in the exam room. Laws and Regulations Applicable to General Contracting in the State of North CarolinaA study publication addressing laws, rules, licensing responsibilities, and regulatory requirements applicable to general contractors in North Carolina. This book is not allowed in the exam room. No physical reference books are included with this online course. Students must obtain the approved exam-room references separately. The study-only books may be useful during preparation, but they cannot be used during the examination. Exam Room Approved Books Only the following two references are identified as approved for use during the North Carolina Insulation Contractor Exam: North Carolina Occupational Safety and Health Standards for the Construction Industry, with latest available amendments North Carolina Energy Conservation Code, 2018 Edition The Contractor’s Guide to Business, Law and Project Management, Insulation Handbook, and Laws and Regulations Applicable to General Contracting in the State of North Carolina are study references only. They are not allowed in the exam room. Candidates should clearly separate permitted books from study-only materials before exam day. Each approved book should also be reviewed for compliance with the current testing provider’s policies on tabs, notes, highlighting, inserts, and bindings. Test Information and Study Materials Begin preparation by dividing the material into practical study categories. Useful areas may include energy-code terminology, thermal resistance, insulation placement, building-envelope continuity, air leakage, installation quality, construction hazards, personal protective equipment, fall protection, access equipment, material handling, and general jobsite safety. Develop a reference map for the two approved books. The safety standards should be associated with workplace conditions, worker protection, construction hazards, and required precautions. The energy conservation code should be associated with insulation requirements, energy-efficiency provisions, thermal-envelope rules, tables, definitions, and compliance conditions. Use practice questions to strengthen both knowledge and lookup speed. Before opening a book, identify the main subject of the question. Then select the most likely reference and search using the exact term or a related keyword. A question may use language that differs slightly from the book, so candidates should recognize common synonyms and technical phrases. Pay close attention to words such as minimum, maximum, required, prohibited, permitted, except, before, and after. These terms can change the correct answer. Read the entire question and all available answer choices before making a selection. Tables and exceptions deserve special attention. Energy-code questions may require candidates to interpret a table, identify a climate-related requirement, or recognize when an exception applies. Safety questions may ask for a required protective measure, a prohibited condition, or a responsibility associated with a particular hazard. Practice under timed conditions as the examination approaches. Use only the approved books and simulate the process of reading the question, identifying the subject, locating the applicable section, and confirming the answer. Timed preparation helps reveal which topics and references need more review. Field experience is valuable, but exam questions may rely on published code language or safety standards rather than a method commonly used by a particular employer. Connect practical experience with the requirements found in the approved references. How 1 Exam Prep Helps You Reach Your Goal 1 Exam Prep helps candidates turn a specialized contractor examination into a clear, manageable study plan. Insulation work combines trade knowledge, energy-code requirements, and construction-safety responsibilities. A structured course helps students approach these subjects in a logical sequence instead of studying without direction. The course supports trade-focused review by emphasizing concepts connected with insulation installation, thermal performance, energy conservation, and safe construction practices. Students can revisit challenging subjects throughout the access period and organize preparation around the areas that need the most attention. Reference navigation is especially important for an open-book examination. 1 Exam Prep encourages candidates to learn how the approved books are arranged, how to use indexes and tables of contents, and how to recognize the type of question that belongs in each reference. Practice-oriented preparation helps students move beyond simple memorization. Candidates can work on identifying key terms, interpreting question wording, distinguishing between similar answer choices, and confirming information in the appropriate book. The 6-month course-access period allows students to build a steady preparation schedule around work and personal responsibilities. Repeated review and book-lookup practice can improve familiarity, reduce confusion, and support greater confidence when approaching the examination. 1 Exam Prep provides educational preparation and study organization. It does not guarantee an examination result, license approval, or a specific professional outcome. Frequently Asked Questions Is the North Carolina Insulation Contractor Exam open book? Yes. The approved references are the North Carolina Occupational Safety and Health Standards for the Construction Industry with the latest available amendments and the North Carolina Energy Conservation Code, 2018 Edition. Are all of the books listed on this page allowed during the exam? No. Only the two titles listed in the Exam Room Approved Books section are permitted. description: North Carolina Grading and Excavating Contractor Highlighted & Tabbed Book Package Prepare for the North Carolina Grading and Excavating Contractor examination with a complete, professionally organized reference package designed for efficient study and faster information retrieval. Every book and reference in this package is highlighted and tabbed to help you locate important safety standards, grading requirements, excavation principles, erosion-control rules, licensing regulations, and other testable material without spending valuable study time creating your own navigation system. This package contains the two references currently approved for use inside the North Carolina Grading and Excavating Contractor examination room, along with six additional references used for study and exam preparation. The additional books are important sources of trade, legal, safety, and regulatory knowledge, but they are not permitted inside the examination room for this classification. The highlighting identifies key provisions, definitions, tables, procedures, and subject areas that deserve attention during preparation. Permanent tabs divide the references into practical sections so you can move between topics more efficiently. This organized format is especially useful for an open-book contractor examination, where success depends not only on understanding the material but also on knowing where information is located. The North Carolina Grading and Excavating classification covers work involving the digging, moving, and placement of earth materials. Its scope includes cuts, fills, excavation, grading, trenching, backfilling, clearing and grubbing, earthen-dam work, and erosion-control activities. The examination therefore draws from several knowledge areas, including excavation practices, construction safety, regulations, utility-location responsibilities, licensing requirements, lien law, and sedimentation control. This highlighted and tabbed package gives candidates an organized foundation for studying those subjects. It is intended for contractors, qualifiers, supervisors, estimators, project managers, and construction professionals preparing to demonstrate their knowledge of grading and excavation work under North Carolina requirements. The package includes both exam-room-approved references and study-only references. Candidates should take only the approved books into the testing room. Exam Details The North Carolina Grading and Excavating Contractor examination is administered by PSI for the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors. Eligibility to take the examination is determined by the licensing board. Examination classification: H — Grading and Excavating Number of scored questions: 45 Time allowed: 120 minutes Passing score: 70% Testing format: Computer-based examination Testing provider: PSI Services LLC The published examination content outline assigns questions to the following subject areas: General Knowledge and Regulations: 9 questions Excavating and Grading: 18 questions Safety — Code of Federal Regulations: 6 questions Lien Law: 1 question Licensing and Regulations: 2 questions One Call: 3 questions Erosion and Sedimentation Control: 6 questions The largest part of the examination focuses on excavation and grading, but candidates should not overlook the smaller categories. Safety, utility-location procedures, sedimentation control, licensing rules, and lien requirements can make the difference between a passing and failing score. PSI may also include a small number of experimental questions. These questions are not scored. Candidates receive their examination results after completing the test, and a score of at least 70% is required to pass. All included references are professionally highlighted and tabbed. Please allow 15 business days for preparation before the package is ready to ship. Open Book Test The North Carolina Grading and Excavating Contractor examination is an open-book test. However, open book does not mean that every book used for study may be taken into the testing room. Only the references specifically identified as approved for this examination classification are allowed. Candidates are responsible for bringing their approved references to the examination center. PSI permits approved books to be highlighted, underlined, and indexed before the examination. Tabs must be permanent and may not be easily removed from the pages. Removable flags and temporary notes are not accepted. Notes may not be written on the tabs. Loose papers and additional attached materials are not permitted. References may not be written in during the examination session. Candidates should review the current PSI Candidate Information Bulletin before test day and make sure their books continue to meet all examination-center rules. The organization provided in this package is valuable because the examination allows approximately two minutes and forty seconds per scored question. Candidates must read the question, determine whether a reference lookup is necessary, find the relevant section, evaluate the available answers, and submit a response within the overall testing period. Familiarity with the tabs and highlighted sections should be developed before exam day. Licensing Steps Choose the appropriate classification and limitation. Determine that the Grading and Excavating classification matches the work the company intends to perform and select the appropriate license limitation for the business. Identify the qualifier. A North Carolina general contractor license must be connected to an individual who has passed the examination approved for the requested classification. This person is known as the qualifier or qualifying party. Complete the license application. Submit the required application information to the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors through its current application process. Provide the required supporting information. The board evaluates matters such as age, character, financial responsibility, applicable fees, and any required background information. Receive examination eligibility. After the application or examination request is approved, the candidate receives an eligibility letter and instructions for registering with PSI. Schedule and take the examination. Use the assigned eligibility information to register, pay the examination fee, select a testing location, and schedule the examination within the authorized eligibility period. Complete the licensing process. Passing the examination satisfies the testing component, but the board must complete its review before issuing the license. Candidates should follow the current instructions provided by the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors and PSI because application procedures, forms, testing policies, and administrative requirements may be revised. State Requirements Applicants seeking a North Carolina general contractor license must submit an application to the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors. Before becoming entitled to an examination, an applicant must be at least 18 years old, possess good moral character as determined by the board, provide evidence of financial responsibility, submit the appropriate application fee, and consent to a criminal background check when required. The business must designate a qualifier who has passed an examination accepted by the board for the applicable classification. The qualifier’s examination is intended to evaluate the practical application of contracting knowledge, including plans and specifications, estimating, construction practices, ethics, state laws, contractor responsibilities, and erosion and sedimentation-control requirements. The Grading and Excavating specialty classification covers the digging, moving, and placement of earth materials using hand tools, powered tools, and equipment commonly associated with excavation and grading operations. The classification includes cuts, fills, trenches, backfilling, clearing, grubbing, erosion-control activities, work on earthen dams, and the use of explosives when connected with covered operations. In North Carolina, a general contractor license is generally required when a person or business bids on, contracts for, or constructs a qualifying project valued at $40,000 or more. The exact classification and license limitation must be appropriate for the work and project value. Reference Books This package contains eight highlighted and tabbed references. It supports preparation for questions involving excavation safety, trenching, protective systems, equipment, worksite hazards, and federal construction-safety requirements. North Carolina Standard Specifications for Roads and Structures, 2018Exam Room Approved. Published by the North Carolina Department of Transportation, this reference addresses standards for roadway and structural construction. It supports preparation involving earthwork, excavation, embankments, materials, grading operations, measurement, construction requirements, and related specifications. North Carolina Administrative Code, Title 15A, Chapter 4 Sedimentation Control, Including the Latest AmendmentsStudy Only — Not Allowed in the Exam Room. This reference contains administrative rules related to sedimentation pollution control. It is useful for studying erosion-control responsibilities, land-disturbing activities, plans, enforcement provisions, inspections, and compliance requirements. North Carolina General Statutes Chapter 113A, Article 4 Sedimentation Pollution Control Act of 1973Study Only — Not Allowed in the Exam Room. This statutory material covers North Carolina’s Sedimentation Pollution Control Act, including the legal framework for controlling sedimentation resulting from land-disturbing activities. North Carolina Excavation Safety Guidelines, 2022 or LaterStudy Only — Not Allowed in the Exam Room. This guide supports preparation for safe excavation and damage-prevention practices, including underground-facility notification, marking, communication, and responsibilities associated with North Carolina’s One Call system. Contractor’s Guide to Business, Law and Project Management — North Carolina General Contractors Edition, 10th EditionStudy Only — Not Allowed in the Exam Room. This North Carolina contractor reference addresses licensing, business organization, project administration, contracts, liens, risk management, employment topics, financial management, and other business-law subjects relevant to general contractors. Pipe and Excavation ContractingStudy Only — Not Allowed in the Exam Room. This trade reference covers excavation operations, soils, trenching, grading, equipment selection, productivity, pipe installation, estimating concepts, and field procedures commonly encountered in underground and earthwork construction. Laws and Regulations Applicable to General Contracting in the State of North CarolinaStudy Only — Not Allowed in the Exam Room. Published by the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors, this reference contains statutes and administrative rules governing general contracting, licensing classifications, qualifiers, limitations, responsibilities, and board procedures. North Carolina Standard Specifications for Roads and Structures, 2018This is the approved construction-specifications reference for the examination. Test Information and Study Materials Begin preparation with the official examination content outline. Allocate the most study time to excavating and grading because it represents 18 of the 45 scored questions. Review terminology, soil and earthwork principles, excavation methods, equipment applications, trenching, backfilling, compaction, grading calculations, and common field practices. Safety is another major area. Learn how to navigate the occupational safety reference and locate requirements involving excavations, trenches, access and egress, protective systems, inspections, material placement, mobile equipment, and worksite hazards. Avoid relying on memory alone when the approved safety book provides a specific regulatory answer. Study erosion and sedimentation control from both the administrative rules and the governing statutes. Although those references are not allowed in the examination room, the topic accounts for six questions. Candidates should understand the purpose of sedimentation-control requirements, regulated land-disturbing activities, plan responsibilities, enforcement concepts, and contractor obligations. One Call procedures account for three questions. Review excavation-notification responsibilities, locate requests, markings, tolerance-zone awareness, emergency situations, and communications with underground-facility operators. A well-organized reference system is most effective when combined with knowledge of the books’ structure. The package supports efficient review of grading, excavation, safety, specifications, erosion control, business law, licensing, utility-location procedures, and North Carolina contractor regulations. The examination includes subjects that require advance study, including sedimentation control, One Call requirements, licensing, lien law, regulations, and general excavation knowledge. The references are organized with permanent tabs. PSI rules do not permit removable tabs such as Post-it flags, and notes may not be written on the tabs. Please allow 15 days for the highlighting and tabbing process before the package is ready to ship. Does purchasing this package register me for the exam? No. Examination eligibility, registration, scheduling, application processing, and licensing are handled separately through the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors and PSI. Does this package guarantee that I will pass? No. Examination results depend on the candidate’s knowledge, preparation, study habits, reference familiarity, and performance on test day. The package provides an organized set of study and exam-room materials to support preparation. Should I study the books that are not allowed in the exam room? Yes. Those references contain important material related to erosion and sedimentation control, excavation safety, utility-location procedures, contractor law, licensing, and trade practices. Candidates should study that information before arriving at the testing center.

title: North Carolina Highway Contractor Highlighted & Tabbed Book Package
description: North Carolina Highway Contractor Highlighted & Tabbed Book Package Prepare for the North Carolina Highway Contractor examination with a comprehensive collection of professionally highlighted and tabbed references. This package combines the six books permitted in the examination room with eleven additional study references covering the major technical, legal, safety, and regulatory subjects associated with highway construction. The North Carolina Highway Contractor examination covers a wide range of work, including asphalt paving, concrete paving, excavation and grading, bridge-related construction, piles, concrete reinforcement, tunneling, railroad construction, marine construction, traffic control, erosion and sedimentation control, sports fields, licensing, liens, and business law. Because the examination draws from many different construction disciplines, candidates need an organized study system and a clear understanding of which references may be used during the test. Every reference in this package is highlighted and tabbed to help direct your attention to important concepts and make key sections easier to locate. The tabs divide large technical books into practical subject areas, while the highlighting identifies definitions, procedures, tables, specifications, safety provisions, construction methods, and regulatory information that may be useful during preparation. The package is divided into two groups. The first group contains the six references approved for use in the North Carolina Highway Contractor examination room. The second group contains eleven study-only books that support preparation but are not permitted inside the testing center for this classification. Keeping these groups clearly separated helps prevent candidates from mistakenly bringing an unapproved reference to the examination. This package is designed for contractors, qualifiers, project managers, estimators, supervisors, engineers, and construction professionals preparing for the North Carolina Highway Contractor examination. It provides a structured way to study a broad classification without beginning with an unorganized stack of technical references. All books require professional preparation before shipment. Please allow 15 business days for the highlighting and tabbing process. Exam Details The North Carolina Highway Contractor examination is administered by PSI for the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors. Candidates must receive examination eligibility through the licensing board before registering and scheduling a testing appointment. Examination classification: Highway Contractor Number of scored questions: 90 Passing score: 70% Time allowed: 265 minutes Testing format: Computer-based examination Testing provider: PSI Services LLC The published content outline distributes the 90 scored questions across the following subject areas: Paving — Asphalt: 12 questions Piles: 5 questions Excavation and Grading: 8 questions Concrete Paving: 3 questions Safety: 5 questions One Call: 3 questions Traffic Control: 2 questions Concrete: 6 questions Metals, Including Concrete Reinforcement: 5 questions Erosion and Sedimentation Control: 4 questions Tunneling: 8 questions Railroad Construction: 8 questions Marine Construction: 6 questions Licensing: 2 questions Liens: 1 question Business and Law: 7 questions Sports Fields: 5 questions The examination may also contain a small number of experimental questions that are not scored. Candidates should prepare for the entire published content outline rather than concentrating only on asphalt paving. Tunneling, railroad work, excavation, business law, concrete, marine construction, reinforcement, safety, and sports-field construction collectively represent a substantial portion of the test. Open Book Test The North Carolina Highway Contractor examination is an open-book test. However, candidates may use only the references specifically approved for this examination classification. Six books in this package are designated as exam-room-approved references. The remaining eleven books are included for study and must not be taken into the testing room. Approved references may be highlighted, underlined, and indexed before the examination. Tabs must be permanent and firmly attached to the pages. Removable flags, temporary notes, loose papers, and easily detached tabs are not permitted. Notes may not be written on the tabs, and candidates may not write in their references during the examination session. The CAMA Handbook must be complete and bound when taken into the testing center. A downloaded copy may be spiral bound or hole-punched and placed in a binder, but partial copies are not accepted. Candidates are responsible for bringing their own approved books to the examination. The 265-minute testing period provides an average of slightly less than three minutes per scored question. That time includes reading each question, reviewing the available answers, performing calculations when needed, finding information in a reference, and submitting a response. Effective preparation therefore requires more than owning the correct books. Candidates should practice navigating the approved references before test day. Licensing Steps Select the Highway Contractor classification. Confirm that the classification matches the construction services the company intends to offer. Choose the appropriate license limitation. North Carolina general contractor licenses are issued with limitations that affect the value of projects the licensee may undertake. Designate a qualifier. The applicant must identify an individual who has passed an examination approved by the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors for the requested classification. Submit the application or examination request. Complete the current licensing documents required by the board and provide the requested supporting information. Meet the board’s applicant requirements. The applicant must satisfy the applicable age, character, financial-responsibility, fee, and background-check provisions. Receive examination eligibility. After approval, the candidate receives an eligibility letter containing the information needed to register with PSI. Register and schedule the examination. Contact PSI within the eligibility period, pay the required examination fee, and select an available testing appointment. Take and pass the Highway Contractor examination. A score of at least 70% is required. Complete the board’s licensing process. Passing the examination completes the testing requirement, but the license is issued only after the board completes its application review. An examination result does not independently authorize a person or company to perform licensed contracting work. The business entity must hold the appropriate active license issued by the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors. State Requirements A North Carolina general contractor license is generally required when a person or business bids on, contracts for, or undertakes a construction project valued at $40,000 or more. The law applies to covered work involving buildings, highways, public utilities, grading, improvements, and structures. Before becoming entitled to an examination, an applicant must be at least 18 years old, possess good moral character as determined by the board, provide evidence of financial responsibility, submit the appropriate application fee, and consent to a criminal background check when required. The applicant must identify a qualifier or qualifying party who has passed an examination accepted by the board. The qualifier demonstrates knowledge related to construction practices, plans and specifications, estimating, ethics, contractor responsibilities, state laws, liens, and erosion and sedimentation control. The Highway Contractor classification covers highway construction activities such as grading, paving, exterior artificial athletic surfaces, bridge construction and repair, culvert work, sidewalks, curbs, gutters, storm drainage, parking decks, guardrails, fencing, signage, and related highway hardware. It also includes paving and grading for airport runways, taxiways, and aprons, along with associated fencing, markings, signage, and runway-lighting work. The scope also incorporates work performed under several related specialty classifications, including boring and tunneling, concrete construction, marine construction, railroad construction, and grading and excavating. This broad scope explains why the examination contains questions from many different construction disciplines. Reference Books This package includes seventeen professionally highlighted and tabbed references. Six are approved for use inside the examination room, while eleven are provided for study only. Sports Fields Design, Construction and Maintenance, Second Edition, 2010Exam Room Approved. Covers the planning, construction, drainage, grading, soil preparation, turf establishment, irrigation, and maintenance of sports fields and exterior athletic surfaces. Contractor’s Guide to Business, Law and Project Management — North Carolina General Contractors Edition, 10th EditionExam Room Approved. Addresses North Carolina contractor licensing, business organization, contracts, project management, financial administration, risk, insurance, employment, liens, and other business-law subjects. North Carolina Standard Specifications for Roads and Structures, 2018Exam Room Approved. Contains North Carolina Department of Transportation requirements for roadway and structural construction, including earthwork, asphalt, concrete, materials, structures, drainage, measurement, and construction procedures. North Carolina Occupational Safety and Health Standards for the Construction Industry, with Latest Available AmendmentsExam Room Approved. Provides construction safety requirements involving excavation, equipment, fall protection, cranes, personal protective equipment, traffic exposure, concrete work, tunneling, and other workplace hazards. Construction Planning, Equipment, and Methods, 10th EditionExam Room Approved. Explains construction planning, production, equipment selection, earthmoving, excavation, hauling, compaction, concrete operations, cranes, piles, tunneling, and construction methods. CAMA Handbook for Development of Coastal North CarolinaExam Room Approved. Provides guidance on development within North Carolina’s regulated coastal areas, including permits, areas of environmental concern, shoreline activities, docks, erosion, and coastal-development responsibilities. North Carolina Administrative Code, Title 15A, Chapter 4 Sedimentation Control, Including the Latest AmendmentsStudy Only — Not Allowed in the Exam Room. Contains administrative rules governing erosion and sedimentation control for land-disturbing activities in North Carolina. North Carolina General Statutes Chapter 113A, Article 4 Sedimentation Pollution Control Act of 1973Study Only — Not Allowed in the Exam Room. Contains the statutory framework for controlling sedimentation caused by land-disturbing construction activities. North Carolina Excavation Safety Guidelines, 2022 or LaterStudy Only — Not Allowed in the Exam Room. Supports preparation for North Carolina One Call and safe-digging questions involving underground utilities, notification, markings, communication, and excavation responsibilities. Pipe and Excavation ContractingStudy Only — Not Allowed in the Exam Room. Reviews excavation, trenching, soils, dewatering, pipe installation, grading, equipment, production, estimating, backfilling, and compaction practices. Design and Control of Concrete Mixtures, 17th EditionStudy Only — Not Allowed in the Exam Room. Covers concrete materials, mixture proportioning, durability, testing, placement, curing, strength, admixtures, and quality-control principles. Hot Mix Asphalt Paving HandbookStudy Only — Not Allowed in the Exam Room. Explains asphalt-mixture production, hauling, placement, compaction, paving operations, equipment, quality control, and common pavement-construction issues. Laws and Regulations Applicable to General Contracting in the State of North CarolinaStudy Only — Not Allowed in the Exam Room. Contains statutes and administrative rules governing North Carolina general contractor licensing, qualifiers, classifications, limitations, renewals, responsibilities, and enforcement. Placing Reinforcing BarsStudy Only — Not Allowed in the Exam Room. Addresses reinforcing-bar materials, detailing, supports, placement tolerances, splices, field practices, and reinforcement for concrete construction. Training and Certification of Field Personnel for Unbonded Post-Tensioning — Level 1 Field FundamentalsStudy Only — Not Allowed in the Exam Room. Introduces field procedures, components, installation practices, stressing operations, safety considerations, and inspection fundamentals for unbonded post-tensioning systems. Jacked Tunnel Design and Construction, 1999Study Only — Not Allowed in the Exam Room. Reviews planning, design, ground behavior, equipment, shafts, alignment, jacking forces, pipe-jacking operations, and construction considerations for jacked tunnels. The Practical Guide to Railway Engineering, 3rd Edition, 2019Study Only — Not Allowed in the Exam Room. Provides an overview of railroad engineering, including track, subgrade, drainage, structures, construction, maintenance, operations, and railway-system fundamentals. Exam Room Approved Books The following six references from this package are approved for use inside the North Carolina Highway Contractor examination room: Sports Fields Design, Construction and Maintenance, Second Edition, 2010Used for questions related to exterior athletic surfaces and sports-field design, construction, grading, drainage, and maintenance. Contractor’s Guide to Business, Law and Project Management — North Carolina General Contractors Edition, 10th EditionUsed for business law, licensing, liens, contracts, project administration, and contractor-management subjects. North Carolina Standard Specifications for Roads and Structures, 2018Used for roadway specifications, paving, grading, drainage, concrete, materials, structures, and construction requirements. North Carolina Occupational Safety and Health Standards for the Construction Industry, with Latest Available AmendmentsUsed for construction-safety questions and precise occupational safety requirements. Construction Planning, Equipment, and Methods, 10th EditionUsed for construction equipment, production, excavation, earthmoving, piles, tunneling, concrete operations, and construction methods. CAMA Handbook for Development of Coastal North CarolinaUsed for coastal-development and marine-construction subjects. The complete reference must be properly bound before it is taken into the examination center. The eleven remaining references are study materials only. They should be reviewed during preparation, but they are not permitted inside the examination room for the Highway Contractor test. Test Information and Study Materials Begin with the published content outline and divide your study schedule according to the number of questions assigned to each topic. Asphalt paving is the largest single category, but focusing only on paving would leave most of the examination uncovered. Tunneling, railroad construction, excavation and grading, concrete, marine construction, reinforcement, business law, safety, piles, sports fields, and erosion control all require dedicated review. For asphalt preparation, study materials, plant operations, transportation, paver operation, grade and slope control, joints, segregation, compaction, temperature, rolling patterns, density, surface defects, and quality-control practices. Use the road specifications to understand how requirements are presented and practice locating applicable sections quickly. For excavation and grading, review soil characteristics, cut-and-fill operations, equipment production, hauling, compaction, slopes, trenches, drainage, dewatering, and underground utility precautions. The construction-equipment reference and the study-only excavation books can help candidates connect theoretical questions with field practices. Tunneling and railroad construction account for sixteen questions combined. Study tunneling methods, shafts, support, jacking, ground conditions, equipment, safety, track components, subgrade, ballast, drainage, alignment, railroad structures, and construction procedures. These sections deserve meaningful preparation even when a candidate’s primary work experience is in conventional paving. Review concrete materials, mixture properties, placement, curing, paving, reinforcement, splices, supports, and post-tensioning fundamentals. The concrete and reinforcement books are not permitted in the examination room, so the most important principles from those references should be learned during preparation. Use the approved references under timed conditions. Practice identifying the subject of a question before opening a book. Select the most likely reference, use the permanent tabs to reach the correct section, and confirm the answer from the text or table. Repeated navigation practice helps reduce unnecessary searching during the test. Study the non-approved books rather than ignoring them. Their subjects appear in the content outline even though the books cannot be brought into the exam. Erosion control, One Call responsibilities, asphalt practices, concrete technology, reinforcement, post-tensioning, tunneling, railway engineering, excavation, licensing, and lien law all require advance preparation. How 1 Exam Prep Helps You Reach Your Goal 1 Exam Prep helps candidates organize a demanding examination with professionally prepared references and trade-focused study guidance. The highlighted and tabbed books reduce the time required to create a reference-navigation system from the beginning and provide a more structured starting point for preparation. Highlighting draws attention to important definitions, requirements, procedures, tables, and technical concepts while still encouraging candidates to read and understand the surrounding material. The package also makes a clear distinction between exam-room-approved books and study-only books. This helps candidates prepare with the full reference library while knowing exactly which six references may be used during the examination. 1 Exam Prep supports practice-oriented preparation through organized study structure, reference navigation, trade review, and repeated lookup exercises. Candidates can use the prepared books to develop familiarity with where information appears and how different examination subjects connect to the approved references. No study package can guarantee a passing score, licensing approval, or a particular examination outcome. Consistent preparation, practical experience, careful reading, and familiarity with the references remain essential. An organized package can help candidates use their study time more effectively and approach the examination with greater confidence. Frequently Asked Questions How many books are included in this package? The package includes seventeen highlighted and tabbed references. Six are approved for use inside the examination room, and eleven are included for study only. Are all seventeen books allowed in the exam? No. Only the six books listed in the Exam Room Approved Books section may be taken into the North Carolina Highway Contractor examination room. The examination includes several subjects whose primary study references are not permitted in the testing room. These books help candidates learn the material before exam day. Can I use removable tabs or Post-it flags? No. Exam references must use permanent tabs that are not easily removed. Temporary flags and removable tabs are not permitted. Can I write notes in the books? The examination rules permit approved references to be highlighted, underlined, and indexed before the test, but written notes and loose attached materials are not permitted. Candidates may not write in the books during the examination. Does the package include exam registration? No. Licensing applications, eligibility approval, examination registration, testing fees, and appointment scheduling are handled separately through the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors and PSI. Does this package guarantee a passing score? description: North Carolina Insulation Contractor Highlighted & Tabbed Book Package Prepare for the North Carolina Insulation Contractor examination with a professionally organized collection of highlighted and tabbed reference books. The North Carolina Insulation Contractor examination covers both technical trade knowledge and contractor responsibilities. Candidates are expected to understand insulation materials, thermal performance, radiant and reflective barriers, vapor retarders, workplace safety, liens, and North Carolina laws and regulations. The Contractor’s Guide to Business, Law and Project Management, Insulation Handbook, and Laws and Regulations Applicable to General Contracting in the State of North Carolina are included for preparation but are not allowed in the examination room. Exam Details The North Carolina Insulation Contractor examination is administered by PSI for the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors. Candidates must first receive examination eligibility from the licensing board before registering and scheduling a PSI testing appointment. Classification: Specialty Contractor — Insulation Number of scored questions: 40 Passing score: 70% Time allowed: 90 minutes Testing format: Computer-based examination Testing provider: PSI Services LLC The examination content outline divides the 40 scored questions among the following subject areas: General Knowledge and Principles: 10 questions Liens: 1 question Insulation Types and Properties: 15 questions Radiant and Reflective Barriers and Vapor Retarders: 7 questions Safety: 5 questions Laws and Regulations: 2 questions Insulation types and properties represent the largest portion of the examination. Candidates should understand how common insulation products differ in composition, installation method, thermal performance, moisture behavior, fire characteristics, and appropriate application. General insulation knowledge and principles also make up a significant portion of the test. Radiant barriers, reflective insulation systems, and vapor retarders account for seven questions. These topics require candidates to understand heat transfer, moisture movement, placement considerations, facing materials, air spaces, and the conditions under which different products are used. Safety, laws, regulations, and lien questions make up a smaller portion of the examination, but they should not be ignored. A candidate who studies only insulation products may be unprepared for questions involving construction-site hazards, protective equipment, licensing obligations, contractor responsibilities, and lien concepts. Open Book Test The North Carolina Insulation Contractor examination is an open-book test. Only the references specifically approved for this classification may be taken into the examination room. In this package, those references are the North Carolina Occupational Safety and Health Standards for the Construction Industry and the North Carolina Energy Conservation Code, 2018 Edition. The three remaining books are study references and are not allowed inside the testing room. Candidates should use those books to learn the material before exam day rather than planning to rely on them during the examination. Approved reference materials may be highlighted, underlined, and indexed before the examination session. Tabs must be permanent and firmly attached to the pages. Removable index flags, temporary tabs, and Post-it-style markers are not accepted. Notes may not be written on the tabs. References may not contain loose papers or attached supplemental materials. Candidates may not write in the books before or during the examination in a manner prohibited by PSI. Any downloaded building-code reference taken into the testing center must be complete and properly bound. Partial copies are not accepted. The 90-minute testing period provides an average of approximately two minutes and fifteen seconds per scored question. That time includes reading the question, evaluating the answer choices, performing any necessary calculations, locating code or safety information, and submitting a response. Efficient reference navigation is therefore an important part of preparation. Practice using the tabs before test day. Candidates should know where to find insulation requirements, thermal-performance provisions, climate-related criteria, safety standards, definitions, and tables without searching through every chapter. The value of a highlighted and tabbed book increases when the candidate has repeatedly practiced using its organization. Licensing Steps Select the Insulation specialty classification. Confirm that the classification matches the work the company intends to perform. Choose the appropriate license limitation. North Carolina general contractor licenses are issued with limitations that determine the value of projects the licensee may undertake. Identify the qualifier. The applicant must designate an individual who will qualify the license by passing an examination accepted for the requested classification. Submit the required application or examination request. Complete the current forms required by the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors and provide the requested supporting information. Meet the applicant requirements. The board reviews matters such as age, character, financial responsibility, applicable fees, and required background information. Receive examination eligibility. After approval, the candidate receives an eligibility letter and instructions for registering with PSI. Register and schedule the test. Use the assigned eligibility information to select an examination date and testing location within the authorized eligibility period. Take and pass the examination. A score of at least 70% is required to pass the North Carolina Insulation Contractor examination. Complete the licensing process. Passing the exam completes the testing component, but the board must finish reviewing the application before a license is issued. Passing the examination does not by itself authorize a person or company to perform licensed contracting work. The contracting business must hold the appropriate active license issued by the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors. State Requirements North Carolina requires a general contractor license when a person or business bids on, contracts for, or undertakes covered construction work valued at $40,000 or more. The required license must include a classification and limitation appropriate for the proposed work and project value. The Insulation specialty classification covers the installation, alteration, and repair of materials classified as insulating media when those materials are used for the non-mechanical control of temperatures in residential and commercial building construction. This specialty classification does not include insulation applied to mechanical equipment or the ancillary lines and piping connected to that equipment. Candidates should understand this distinction when determining whether work falls within the scope of the Insulation classification. North Carolina applicants must satisfy the licensing board’s requirements before receiving a license. These requirements include submitting the applicable application, identifying a qualifying individual, demonstrating the required financial responsibility, paying the required fees, and completing any required background-review process. The qualifier is the individual whose examination supports the requested classification. The qualifier should understand the trade scope, applicable code requirements, safety responsibilities, contractor laws, and professional obligations associated with the work. License limitations determine the maximum value of a single project that a contractor may undertake. Applicants should select the limitation that fits the company’s financial qualifications and expected project size. Classification and limitation are separate parts of the North Carolina licensing structure. Reference Books This package includes five professionally highlighted and tabbed references. General knowledge and principles account for 10 questions. Study the movement of heat through conduction, convection, and radiation. Understand how insulation affects heat flow, how air spaces influence performance, and why workmanship can affect the installed effectiveness of a product. Review common installation problems such as gaps, compression, voids, misalignment, incomplete coverage, blocked ventilation, and improper placement around building components. Candidates should understand why labeled product values do not always equal installed assembly performance when workmanship is poor. Projects can involve wood framing, metal framing, gypsum board, specialty panels, insulation coordination, backing, blocking, openings, fire-resistant assemblies, and preparation for final finishes. The license limitation determines the monetary value of projects the contractor may undertake. The applicant must designate a qualifier whose accepted examination supports the Interior Construction classification. The qualifier demonstrates examination knowledge, while the contractor license is issued to the approved applicant or business entity. North Carolina generally requires a general contractor license when a person or business undertakes covered construction work valued at $40,000 or more. The licensed entity must hold an appropriate classification and a license limitation that permits the value of the project. Interior construction contractors must also comply with applicable permits, inspections, building-code provisions, fire-resistance requirements, accessibility requirements, project specifications, workplace-safety standards, and manufacturer instructions. Exam Details The North Carolina Grading and Excavating Contractor examination is part of the qualification process for contractors seeking the Grading and Excavating classification. Candidates should prepare for technical, regulatory, safety, and business topics connected with earthmoving and site-development work. Candidates should review clearing, grubbing, stripping, cut-and-fill operations, excavation, embankments, trenching, backfilling, soil handling, moisture conditioning, lift placement, compaction, equipment selection, grade control, drainage, slopes, and surface preparation. General knowledge and regulations account for nine questions. Preparation should include construction terminology, project planning, equipment use, material placement, contractor responsibilities, specifications, earthwork methods, jobsite coordination, and common grading and excavation practices. Safety and erosion and sedimentation control account for twelve questions combined. Candidates should review excavation protective systems, soil classification, safe access, spoil placement, heavy-equipment hazards, personal protective equipment, stabilization, sediment barriers, construction entrances, runoff management, slope protection, and maintenance of erosion-control measures. One-call requirements, licensing, regulations, and lien law complete the examination outline. Although these categories contain fewer questions, they remain part of the final score and should be included in a balanced preparation plan. Open Book Test The North Carolina Grading and Excavating Contractor examination is an open-book test. Only the North Carolina Occupational Safety and Health Standards for the Construction Industry and North Carolina Standard Specifications for Roads and Structures, 2018 are identified for use inside the examination room. The six additional rental books are study-only references and should not be taken into the testing center. North Carolina Standard Specifications for Roads and Structures, 2018 supports preparation involving clearing, excavation, earthwork, grading, embankments, drainage, materials, compaction, roadway construction, erosion-control measures, construction procedures, measurement, acceptance, and quality requirements. State Requirements The North Carolina Grading and Excavating classification covers the digging, moving, and placing of materials that form the surface of the earth, excluding air and water. Covered work includes cuts, fills, excavation, grading, trenching, backfilling, and related operations performed with hand tools, power tools, and earthmoving equipment. The classification also includes work on earthen dams and the use of explosives when those activities are performed in connection with covered grading and excavation work. Clearing, grubbing, and erosion-control activities are also included within the classification. Typical projects may involve site clearing, mass excavation, building pads, roadway subgrades, embankments, trenches, drainage preparation, slope construction, backfill, compaction, rough grading, final grading, and stabilization of disturbed areas. The contractor classification determines the type of construction work the licensed business may perform. The license limitation determines the monetary value of individual projects the contractor may undertake. Applicants should select both according to the company’s intended services, financial qualifications, and anticipated project values. The applicant must designate a qualifier whose accepted examination supports the Grading and Excavating classification. The qualifier demonstrates examination knowledge, while the contractor license is issued to the approved applicant or business entity.
